doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: First real bass, a Big Bill Broonzy blues record date, and drums after hours
summary: Ware gets a real bass, records the blues "WPA" with Big Bill, works until daylight, and plays drums for the end of the show.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But that's when I got my first, real bass violin. I was still going to school, high school, junior high, and Buster got a record date for me. I'll never forget this. And I had to get permission from my teacher to make it, although I'm working every night. We worked from, say, about 9 or 10 o' clock at night until the owner said, Mr. Robinson said, "You could go home now." That means if there were 2 people left in the club, we have to play until they got ready to leave, and it might be daylight. I think I was making something like $3 a night -- or $2 a night.

And he was taking half of that for my fiddle. But I enjoyed it; I was getting a world of experience. And Buster had this record date for this guy named Melrose Mellow's, and I didn't realize who the fellow was -- Big Bill -- we made a

record called "WPA" and in later years I found out it was out of print. But I remember I played all that afternoon -- it was all blues, nothing but blues. Big Bill Broonzy. It was all blues dates. I don't know who the other blues guy -- they kept me on it, you know, I was what you might say the house bassist. I think I made $10, which was good money. I made only $10 a week.
But I was in junior high, and every night around 2 o'clock, Mr. Robinson would tell his son, Mundy, he would say, "All right, Mundy, you go on home. Wilbur, you play the rest of the show on drums."

So I had to switch from the bass to drums. I was still playing drums -- always did play drums as well as bass. So I played the rest of the show, and then when I go to school, that's when I started dropping out. I didn't go. I was still working.
